name: Automating the Enterprise with Foundation Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: ECLAIR uses multimodal foundation models to automate enterprise workflows from natural-language descriptions, with initial studies of workflow understanding and completion.

name: IDA: Breaking Barriers in No-code UI Automation Through Large Language Models and Human-Centric Design
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: IDA helps business users create web UI automation through guided demonstrations, a semantic programming model, and a teaching-oriented interface. A prototype user study examines automation creation with enterprise applications by users without programming backgrounds.

name: Beyond Pass or Fail: Multi-Dimensional Benchmarking of Foundation Models for Goal-based Mobile UI Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Sphinx benchmarks foundation models on goal-based mobile UI navigation, using app test cases and a toolkit that identifies different failure modes.

name: BIMgent: Towards Autonomous Building Modeling via Computer-use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: BIMgent plans software-specific workflows and executes GUI actions for building-information modeling. It evaluates multimodal building design and reconstruction tasks in professional authoring software.

name: Are LLM Agents the New RPA? A Comparative Study with RPA Across Enterprise Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The comparison covers three enterprise RPA challenges.
summary: Compares an agent using computer interfaces with UiPath RPA on enterprise data entry, monitoring, and document extraction, measuring speed, reliability, and development effort.

name: InfraMind: A Novel Exploration-based GUI Agentic Framework for Mission-critical Industrial Management
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: InfraMind explores industrial management GUIs using virtual-machine snapshots and builds memory for planning and hierarchical state recognition. Its framework also studies knowledge distillation and safety checks on open-source and commercial data-center management platforms.

name: RISK: A Framework for GUI Agents in E-commerce Risk Management
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RISK combines browser-interaction training data, a benchmark, and reinforcement fine-tuning for e-commerce risk-management workflows. Its trajectories and rewards distinguish individual actions from multi-step stateful tasks involving deeply embedded web content.

name: SCUBA: Salesforce Computer Use Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: SCUBA evaluates enterprise UI navigation and CRM workflows with 300 task instances derived from Salesforce user interviews. Salesforce sandbox execution and milestone-based assessment support comparisons between zero-shot agents and agents given demonstrations.

name: UI-CUBE: Enterprise-Grade Computer Use Agent Benchmarking Beyond Task Accuracy to Operational Reliability
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UI-CUBE evaluates 226 tasks ranging from individual controls to copy-paste and enterprise workflows. Interface variations, multiple resolutions, and application-state validation support diagnosis of operational reliability beyond task accuracy alone.

name: LegalWebAgent: Empowering Access to Justice via LLM-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: LegalWebAgent separates user-needs clarification, webpage browsing, and actions such as form completion or scheduling. A 15-task evaluation studies legal-service workflows relevant to Québec civil-law users, using HTML and screenshot observations.

name: Using GUI Agent for Electronic Design Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-EDA collects more than 2,000 screenshot-answer-action pairs from engineers working across five CAD tools and five physical domains. The accompanying benchmark evaluates more than 30 GUI agents on specialized electronic-design workflows.

name: ProSoftArena: Benchmarking Hierarchical Capabilities of Multimodal Agents in Professional Software Environments
notes: The paper abstract and official full-text sections were reviewed. The full text supports Windows 11 virtual-machine execution, screenshot/state observations, and mouse/keyboard actions.
summary: ProSoftArena evaluates 436 professional-software tasks across six disciplines and 13 applications in a Windows 11 virtual-machine environment. Its capability hierarchy, execution-based checks, and human-in-the-loop evaluation cover precise GUI operations and multi-software workflows.

name: EntWorld: A Holistic Environment and Benchmark for Verifiable Enterprise GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces EntWorld, an enterprise GUI benchmark built by deriving task logic from database schemas. Long workflows across enterprise domains are assessed with deterministic SQL-based state checks rather than screenshot similarity alone.

name: Terminal Agents Suffice for Enterprise Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v4). The subject is terminal agents using APIs; graphical web agents appear as another approach.
summary: Studies enterprise automation by terminal agents that call platform APIs, comparing their task results and cost with other agent approaches, including web agents using graphical interfaces.

name: HealthAdminBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Healthcare Administration Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces HealthAdminBench with GUI environments for an electronic health record, payer portals and fax handling. Expert-defined administrative tasks are decomposed into verifiable subtasks to compare local progress with end-to-end workflow completion.

name: RiskWebWorld: A Realistic Interactive Benchmark for GUI Agents in E-commerce Risk Management
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces RiskWebWorld, an interactive benchmark of e-commerce risk-management tasks for GUI agents on websites, with Gymnasium infrastructure for evaluation and agentic RL.

name: Anchor: Preventing Artifact Drift for Reliable Agent Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The shared verifier scores end-state business correctness across several agent harnesses.
summary: Anchor builds ERP-Bench by generating procurement and manufacturing tasks with shared state verifiers for evaluating browser and computer-use agents.

name: BlueFin: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Financial Spreadsheets
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces BlueFin, a benchmark and evaluation framework for agents handling professional finance spreadsheet workbooks through synthesis, manipulation, and comprehension tasks.

name: SpreadsheetBench 2: Evaluating Agents on End-to-End Business Spreadsheet Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SpreadsheetBench 2, a benchmark of multi-sheet business spreadsheet workflows for agents, covering generation, debugging, and visualization tasks.

name: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a benchmark for long-horizon office-suite agent tasks with labor-time and price signals, plus rubric-based code verifiers.

name: FinCUABuild: Can Agents Build Reliable Benchmarks for Dynamic Financial Computer Use?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported qualification rates are measured on FinCUABuildBench.
summary: Introduces FinCUABuildBench for assessing financial computer-use task construction and FinCUABuildAgent for generating tasks, environments, and validators.

name: WaitLens: Temporal VLM-Based Adaptive Waiting for Industrial GUI Testing Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its waiting-time evaluation uses recordings from an industrial testing pipeline.
summary: Introduces WaitLens, a vision-language model trained on GUI loading trajectories to decide when testing agents can stop waiting for an interface to load.

name: Build or Adopt? Custom-Built vs. General-Purpose LLM Agent Harnesses for Automotive GUI Testing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The comparison uses one organization's vehicle test cases, public-app tasks, and practitioner interviews.
summary: Compares a custom harness with general-purpose LLM agent harnesses for GUI testing of Android-based vehicle interfaces and tasks in public apps.

name: CUGA
notes: The README calls it a Configurable Generalist Agent built with IBM; IBM's papers expand the name as Computer Using Generalist Agent. The default task mode is API-only; web and hybrid modes run the browser agent (planner, action agent with click, type, select, go-back and scroll tools, and page understanding) through a browser extension. NOTICE lists files derived from BrowserGym. The README cites arXiv 2510.23856 for its WebArena result; that paper is not in the catalog, and the curated arxiv:2503.01861 describes the CUGA system without naming this repository, so no relation is recorded. Benchmark figures are the publisher's and were not reproduced. Code was read, not run.
summary: Enterprise generalist agent harness that plans over APIs and MCP or OpenAPI tools and, in web or hybrid mode, acts on pages through a browser extension, with intent guards, tool approval and tool guards.

name: Asteroid
notes: The site footer names Entropy Systems, Inc. as the operator. The homepage describes three execution modes: a frontier model reading the screen and acting on first runs, agent-written deterministic scripts for repeat runs, and direct calls to a portal's private API when one is found; it also describes an agent builder (Astro), approval checkpoints and step-by-step run recordings. An August 2026 company blog post says Asteroid has deployed agents built on Anthropic's computer use tool since February 2026 as an early-access participant, and that its agents run on Linux sandboxes and reach Windows-only EHRs through remote desktop. Customer outcome figures, HIPAA and SOC 2 claims, pricing and reliability are publisher statements and were not independently tested. The asteroidai GitHub organization and docs.asteroid.ai were not reviewed.
summary: Hosted healthcare automation platform whose agents operate EHRs, payer portals and Windows, Linux or Citrix apps from the screen, then turn repeat runs into scripts or private-API calls served as an API.

name: AutomotiveUI-Bench-4K
notes: Sparks Solutions publishes one ungated test split of 22 Parquet shards at revision d760810c. The card describes mostly photographs of in-vehicle infotainment displays plus some direct screenshots such as Android Auto; its per-brand image counts cover 13 car brands, Apple CarPlay and Google Android Auto and sum to 998. No catalog platform facet fits infotainment systems, so the environment is unspecified. Each annotation pairs a bounding box with either an imperative test action or an expected-result statement labeled passed or failed; UI text is German or English and annotations are English. The card's example code runs the publisher's ELAM-7B model, and its results table is publisher-reported. The card cites arXiv 2505.05895 (Ernhofer et al., 2025). CC-BY-4.0 is the card's data declaration.
summary: Offline test set of 998 photos and screenshots of in-vehicle infotainment screens from 15 brands, with 4,208 English annotations for locating UI elements and judging expected results as passed or failed.
